results.summary: This is a placeholder design for a counter that counts from 1 to 4, intended for the Wokwi simulation environment. The documentation is essentially a template with no functional description, only pin names suggesting a 7-segment display output and switch inputs. It requires external hardware such as a 7-segment display and switches to be useful. The design is not sufficiently documented to determine its actual behavior or purpose.

The project is titled 'Count To Ten' but the documentation consists only of placeholder text such as 'asdf' and 'dsaf'. The pin names are similarly meaningless, providing no insight into the design's function. There is no description of how it works, how to test it, or what external hardware is needed. The project is essentially undocumented and cannot be evaluated.

This design uses a clock and a binary counter to cycle through the characters O, 2, E, L, H, d, and blank on a 7-segment display, spelling 'O2ELHd'. It is tested by setting the clock to 1 Hz and observing the display, with a reset input to restart the sequence. External hardware includes a 7-segment LED display, a clock source, and a reset button. The design is a simple demonstration of driving a 7-segment display with a counter.

This design displays the custom string 'rESIStcodE' on a 7-segment display. It is tested by connecting a 7-segment display to the outputs and an 8-position DIP switch to the inputs. The external hardware required includes a 7-segment display and a DIP switch. The documentation is minimal and does not explain the internal logic or how the characters are generated.

This is a 4-bit ALU that performs addition, subtraction, AND, and OR operations on two 4-bit inputs, with the operation selected by two mode pins. The result is output on four pins, and an overflow flag is provided. It is tested by applying input numbers and operation codes and checking the outputs against expected results. External hardware includes resistors, LEDs, and DIP switches for input and output. The design is a simple educational example of an ALU.

This design is a simple counter that counts seconds when driven by a 10 kHz oscillator. It has a debugging reset pin but no other documented inputs or outputs. It is tested by enabling the 10 kHz oscillator and observing the counter behavior. No external hardware is required. The documentation is very brief and does not specify the output format or how the count is observed.

The TinyTapeout Signal Box loads switch settings into SRAMs to control outputs, with the desired track selected via DIP switches and loaded by pressing reset. It is designed to work out of the box without external hardware. The design provides multiple output signals based on the stored configuration. The documentation is minimal but indicates a memory-based signal routing function.

This is an educational Wokwi project intended as a starting point for Swiss high school students to learn ASIC design and digital circuitry basics. It includes a 4-bit binary counter and two 4-bit registers with write and read operations controlled by opcode pins. The design is tested by following exercises on the Wokwi project page, which explain how to store and retrieve data. No external hardware is required, and the project serves as a teaching tool with documented pitfalls.

This design is a simple 8-bit SRAM with 8 input and 8 output pins. The documentation is extremely sparse, stating only 'a simple 8-bit SRAM' and 'just do it' for testing, with 'finger(s)' listed as external hardware. There is no explanation of addressing, read/write control, or how the memory is accessed. The design is essentially undocumented beyond its title.

This design checks if a 4-digit BCD input equals 2904 and lights an LED birthday candle if it matches. It uses 8 input pins and 8 bidirectional pins to represent the four BCD digits, with the match output on a single pin. It is tested by setting the digits to 2, 9, 0, 4 and observing the LED, and by trying invalid numbers. External hardware includes an LED for the candle. The design is a simple puzzle or game for a birthday.
